name: center_handle_visibility
description: Frozen reference behaviour for the transform gizmo's CENTRE HANDLE — the grab target drawn at the gizmo origin, distinct from the axis arms and from the action-centre marker underneath it. Three facts: it defaults ON; the item-move configuration turns it OFF; and its state disturbs neither the action centre nor the axis banks. Also records, deliberately, WHICH probe answered the 'is it grabbable' question and which one could not.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted): attribute reads for the default/override, an A/B viewport capture for what is drawn, a hover capture for what is interactive, and a drag capture that turned out not to discriminate.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (scripts, per-case result JSON and four retained screenshots live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: The pixel figures below were RE-DERIVED from the retained screenshots while writing this fixture, not copied from the capture's prose — and the re-derivation corrected it: the capture reported ONE changed viewport cluster, there are two (see drawn.clusters). The centre-handle-off hover leg is the one figure here that could not be re-derived: its screenshots were not retained, so it is marked reported_only.

attribute.comment: The centre handle is a boolean the tool configuration can carry. Read headless off the live tool.
attribute.order_independence_evidence: Both orders were run in one session — base, then item-move, then base again (1, 0, 1); and item-move, then base, then item-move (0, 1, 0). A configuration therefore RESETS attributes it does not itself list, so the item-move configuration's 0 is a real override and not a redundant no-op that happened to agree with a leftover value.
attribute.note: Only the MOVE member of the item-suffixed transform family carries the override; the rotate/scale/combined item members do not.

drawn.comment: A/B screenshot on ONE session: same scene, same camera, only the flag flips. Counts are restricted to the viewport pane [4..908] x [4..966]; the rest of the screen also changes because the properties panel redraws the flag's own row, which is not evidence about the gizmo.

clusters.what: the centre handle itself, at the gizmo origin
clusters.note: When the handle is ON it COVERS the action-centre marker that is what you see when it is OFF — the marker does not move, it is occluded.

Far from the gizmo and unrelated to the axis banks. The capture's prose claimed the gizmo blob was the ONLY in-pane change; re-derivation found this second cluster. It is recorded so nobody re-derives 'exactly one thing changes' from a stale summary.

drawn.axis_arms_evidence: Every changed in-pane pixel falls inside one of the two clusters above. A moved or re-scaled axis arm would produce long streaks along the arm directions; there are none.

interactive.comment: Hover was the channel that separated 'a real grab target' from 'a decoration'.
interactive.hover_px_when_off_note: The capture reported 0 changed pixels when hovering the same point with the handle off. Its screenshots were NOT retained, so unlike every other figure in this block it could not be re-derived here. Treated as reported, not as re-verified.

vacuous_probe.comment: RECORDED ON PURPOSE. A drag test was run first and could not answer grabbability. Do not re-run it, and do not add one like it to a test.
vacuous_probe.probe: press on the centre-handle pixel vs press 375 px away in empty viewport space, with the handle on and off — four cells
vacuous_probe.why_vacuous: This tool free-moves the subject on ANY viewport drag, so 'the centre handle is grabbable' and 'the centre handle is inert' predict the SAME motion. Four bit-identical cells are not agreement between the hypotheses' predictions; they are a channel that cannot disagree.
vacuous_probe.what_worked_instead: hover highlighting — see the interactive block

does_not_disturb.comment: Measured across the two configurations that differ in this flag, on two separate rigs (the single-item pivot rig and the three-item primary rig): the evaluated action-centre and axis packets are bit-identical.

classification.detail: vibe3d reaches the SAME observable by a different mechanism. There is no per-configuration flag here and no item-specific transform configuration at all: one tool branches on whether the subject is items or mesh components, and the centre handle (gizmo part 3) is registered in both branches but reports visible=false in the item branch and visible=true in the component branch. That is exactly the reference's default-on / off-for-item-move pair, so the two observable facts ARE tested live. The axis-banks-undisturbed half is tested live too (the arm and plane parts stay visible in both branches).
not_tested_and_why: The independent toggle does not exist here — the handle's state is bound to the subject type — so the reference's A/B of the ACTION CENTRE across one flag flip cannot be reproduced: vibe3d's two states have different subjects, and their centres legitimately differ (the item branch reads the item pivot, the component branch the geometry). Only the axis-bank half of 'does not disturb' is assertable.
The hover-highlight channel is not read over the test API at the pixel fidelity the reference capture used, so the 'it is a real grab target, not a decoration' fact is frozen here as data only.
